_readme: Provenance for the concatenated 2026-09-15 recording. Trodes was stopped and restarted
that day, so the session exists on disk as two .rec folders; they are one session in
every sense that matters, and this file records exactly how they were joined so that
spike times from the joint sort can be mapped back to each part's own clock and to its
own Bpod file. Sample indices are 30 kHz samples of 384 int16 channels (768 bytes a
sample). Nothing here is inferred from the file names: every number was measured.

why: At t = 4150 s (69.17 min) 82 of the 384 channels jump above three times the
healthy spike-band noise level and stay there for the remaining 112 s. The
is a connector/ground signature rather than anything biological, and is very
probably what forced Trodes to be restarted. The cut is at 4145 s, five seconds
before the fault, so no part of it reaches the sorter: Kilosort estimates
whitening and drift over the whole file, so 112 s of 82 bad channels would
degrade the other 2.16 h rather than just itself.

warning: The seam is a real discontinuity in time, not in the data array. Anything that bins
over time, computes a rate, or looks for drift must treat sample 124350000 as a
break of 37m56s and never interpolate across it. One Kilosort batch straddles the
seam and its spikes should be checked for a rate artefact after sorting.

channel_map: Both parts carry the same Trodes channelmap, and the probe map built from each is
byte-identical: map A, 384 channels, xc 2426-2474, yc 920-4740.
probe_did_not_move: Spike-band (300-6000 Hz, after CAR) per-channel RMS fingerprints over all 384
channels: part 1 at 35 min against part 2 at 30 min gives r = 0.9157. The
within-recording controls are r = 0.9275 (part 1, 1 min vs 35 min) and r = 0.8328
(part 2, start vs end), so across the 38-minute gap the channels see the same thing
as well as they do within a single recording. Best depth lag inside part 2 is 0 rows.
evidence_that_joining_is_sound.gain: 0.018311105685598315 in both parts, read from each .rec header's spikeScalingToUv.

how_to_map_results_back: A spike at concat sample s belongs to part 1 if s < 124350000, with part-1 sample s;
otherwise it belongs to part 2, with part-2 sample s - 124350000. The same offset
applies to the DIO trial markers, which are read from each .rec separately and then
shifted, and to the two Bpod files, whose trials are renumbered continuously with the
supersedes: The standalone sort of 20260915_103710 (LSF 741761, 447 units, review tool
https://claude.ai/artifact/QreYaMjGtujiE17m2k9zXf) covers only part 2 and has no
verdicts in it, so nothing hand-made is lost by replacing it. It stays on Z as a
second opinion; the joint sort's unit ids do not correspond to its.
